page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Substitute t = eˣ
steps.why: eˣ is its own derivative, so eˣdx converts to dt in the simplest possible substitution, leaving a plain sint to integrate.
common_mistakes: Overcomplicating this with integration by parts instead of the direct one-line substitution.
Forgetting that eˣdx (the WHOLE outside factor) equals dt, not just dx.
steps.memory_tip: eˣ is its own derivative — eˣdx = dt directly, no extra chain-rule factor to track.

steps.label: Integrate and back-substitute for the final answer
steps.why: ∫sint dt = −cost + c, and substituting t=eˣ back in gives the final answer as a cosine of eˣ.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to substitute eˣ back in for t.
steps.memory_tip: Same ∫sint=−cost rule as answers 149.1 and 154 — the third time this exact standard result appears in this chapter.
